### adonayjunior/port-billing-tariffs — MIT tiered terminal billing oracle
- URL: https://github.com/adonayjunior/port-billing-tariffs
- Exact commit / revision: `feb1cd5db183fa45047660f5e2e5f4d8ba966fd4`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: strong / Master contender
- What it contains: A generic .NET terminal-billing engine with effective-dated `TariffRate` records for gate-in, gate-out, storage and container handling, plus a separate `DemurrageTariffPlan` that combines free days with contiguous escalating daily tiers. The domain rejects invalid ranges, gaps, overlaps, nonpositive rates and nonfinal open-ended tiers; a rate selector requires exactly one effective rate for a service/date. Inspected tests exercise free-time boundaries and tier arithmetic, including zero through day 5, then escalating charges across later tiers.
- Rare or undernoticed value: Rights-clean independent terminal/accessorial arithmetic is much rarer than generic freight rating. This gives a second deterministic oracle for port storage/demurrage/handling that can challenge the primary stack rather than merely echo it.
- Likely buyer / user: Importers, NVOCCs, forwarders, terminal-billing teams and freight-audit/payment vendors.
- Painful problem: Terminal charges are highly sensitive to free-time boundaries, tier transitions and effective dates; a small rule error can manufacture or miss recoverable dollars.
- Monetization mechanism: Fixed-price terminal-charge diagnostic, managed overcharge recovery, or an embedded deterministic port-charge module.
- Likely first paid wedge: Customer-authorized terminal tariff schedule plus container event history plus billed charge lines -> recomputed expected storage/demurrage/handling -> evidence-linked discrepancy report.
- Build-time or data advantage: Roughly 1–3 months of terminal-billing domain/invariant/test work compressed, with unusually useful tier-boundary tests for an independent oracle.
- Concrete evidence inspected: actual root `LICENSE`; `src/PortBilling.Domain/Tariffs/DemurrageTariffPlan.cs`; `tests/PortBilling.Domain.Tests/DemurrageTariffPlanTests.cs`; exact revision and commit metadata. Repository documentation states the terminal/rates are generic/fictitious rather than copied from a proprietary operator.
- License / rights: MIT verified from the actual repository LICENSE. Fictitious/synthetic tariff examples can be used as software tests; real customer/carrier/terminal schedules still require their own authorization and provenance.
- Reuse classification: Directly reusable under MIT notice requirements.
- Recovery-safety caveat: The inspected demurrage plan repository behaves like one current plan rather than a historically versioned authority, and a closed final tier can leave later days unpriced. A recovery implementation must bind every charge to the controlling version/effective window and route uncovered days to REVIEW/$0 rather than silently stopping or inventing a rate.
- Why it is not already obvious / crowded: Tiny generic port-billing repository with value concentrated in the domain invariants/tests rather than a polished freight-audit product.
- Combination opportunities: Authorized external accessorial schedule -> Qatoto/Trenova versioned authority -> port-billing as independent terminal-charge calculator -> aiparallel/open_tms discrepancy -> four13-style dispute/settlement lineage. It also forms a lawful synthetic benchmark family with the same author's gate/TOS projects.
- Value score: A 4/5; B 4/5; C 4/5; D 4/5; E 5/5; F 5/5 = **26/30**.
- Next action: Add a synthetic benchmark with effective-date changes, weekend/working-day variants, open-ended and deliberately uncovered final tiers; require version provenance and REVIEW/$0 for any unpriced period.

### Aryapd021/DemurrageOS — two-clock container fee engine reference
- URL: https://github.com/Aryapd021/DemurrageOS
- Exact commit / revision: `329d9209ed6e5de5089da9739307cd5913287c16`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: watch / strong clean-room reference
- What it contains: A substantial TypeScript/PostgreSQL container-charge platform with tariff entities, container events, charge/exposure records, audit/outbox infrastructure, worker queues, document/import routes and a financial engine modeling DPD_DIRECT, CFS and DPD_CFS clocks. `TariffEngine.getTariffForDate` selects effective-dated tariffs; `FreeTimeEngine` chooses discharge, CFS gate-in or fallback-event anchors; charge calculation uses Decimal-based money utilities and records calculation inputs/tariff version.
- Rare or undernoticed value: The useful domain idea is the two-clock interpretation of container free time and fallback from direct-port delivery into CFS, a class of event semantics that generic `days x rate` engines omit.
- Likely buyer / user: Importers, customs-house agents, NVOCCs, forwarders and demurrage/detention audit teams.
- Painful problem: Wrong event clock selection can dominate the dollar result even when the rate itself is correct.
- Monetization mechanism: Clean-room container free-time/exposure diagnostic or an event-interpretation module feeding managed recovery.
- Likely first paid wedge: Customer-authorized container event history + controlling tariff -> explain which clock controls free time and calculate reviewable exposure before invoice/payment.
- Build-time or data advantage: Roughly 2–4 months of container-event, tariff, job/audit and operational application design guidance.
- Concrete evidence inspected: exact commit/tree; `apps/api/src/services/financial/charge-calculation.ts`; repository test inventory including `financial.test.ts`; Prisma/application structure. Repository claims of production-readiness/test completeness were treated as repository claims rather than independently executed proof.
- License / rights: No root LICENSE file was present at the inspected revision; no reuse grant established.
- Reuse classification: Inspect / learn / clean-room only unless permission is established.
- Recovery-safety caveat: The inspected calculator can fall back from a missing CFS gate-in to discharge/fallback timestamps, selects an effective tariff without visible carrier/port/container/service scope in that function, uses current wall-clock time internally, and prices simple daily rates. Those behaviors are not acceptable as recovery authority without stronger scoping, deterministic `as_of`, event-evidence requirements and fail-closed REVIEW/$0 behavior.
- Why it is not already obvious / crowded: Newly built low-attention demurrage platform whose value is hidden in event-clock/application structure, but its README is much stronger than its current rights posture.
- Combination opportunities: Opstrax physical truth + clean-room DemurrageOS clock semantics + Qatoto/Trenova tariff version authority + MIT port-billing tier arithmetic -> evidence-backed detention/demurrage discrepancy.
- Value score: A 4/5; B 4/5; C 5/5; D 4/5; E 5/5; F 1/5 = **23/30**.
- Next action: Recreate the DPD/CFS/fallback clock cases synthetically with explicit missing-event hard negatives; do not copy source absent a license.

### ritickchahar/Web-Scrapers — Hapag-Lloyd tariff PDF discovery/extraction reference
- URL: https://github.com/ritickchahar/Web-Scrapers
- Exact commit / revision: `13803dd53ec8e0eeb7cd61aefcbc0ca96a4ccd1a`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: watch / clean-room and rights-check only
- What it contains: Within the Hapag-Lloyd subdirectory, a pipeline stores public tariff-PDF links by region/country, downloads PDFs, extracts text with PyPDF2, asks a model for structured liner/port/currency/effective/expiry/free-day/day-type/equipment/tier data, and persists tariffs, container types and charge buckets (`start_day`, `end_day`, `rate`, `rate_unit`) in SQLite.
- Rare or undernoticed value: It is one of the few public-code examples found that starts from an external carrier tariff-document source rather than assuming the accessorial schedule is already normalized. The schema directly targets the P0 missing-authority lane: effective windows, free-time type and escalating charge buckets.
- Likely buyer / user: Ocean shippers, NVOCCs, forwarders and freight-audit/payment vendors.
- Painful problem: A billed-vs-contracted engine cannot recover terminal/carrier D&D if it cannot lawfully locate, version and prove the controlling external schedule/addendum.
- Monetization mechanism: Clean-room public-source tariff registry and change-monitor feeding a reviewed freight recovery product; not direct reuse of this scraper or third-party tariff documents.
- Likely first paid wedge: For a customer-authorized lane/carrier set, maintain source URLs/hashes/effective dates for applicable public schedules, require analyst confirmation, then rerate only against verified authoritative facts.
- Build-time or data advantage: Roughly 1–2 months of source-discovery/schema requirements and a useful concrete target for free-time/tier extraction.
- Concrete evidence inspected: `Hapag-Lloyd/src/extraction/process_tarffic_pdfs.py`; `Hapag-Lloyd/src/database/database.py`; exact commit and recursive tree. The extraction currently sends model output directly to persistence and does not provide the source-location/evidence gates required by this stack.
- License / rights: No root repository LICENSE was present at the inspected revision. A linked/mentioned license elsewhere is not treated as a grant for this project. Publicly reachable carrier PDFs also remain subject to their own copyright/terms and are not assumed redistributable.
- Reuse classification: Inspect / learn / clean-room only. Do not copy the code or republish tariff documents/values without a valid basis.
- Safety note: The same multi-purpose repository tree exposes unrelated folders suggesting personal-email and leak-oriented scraping material; those files were deliberately not opened, mined or preserved. Inspection was limited to the freight tariff subdirectory and repository metadata.
- Why it is not already obvious / crowded: Freight tariff capability is buried inside a miscellaneous scraper collection and has essentially no product framing.
- Combination opportunities: Independently implemented public/customer-authorized source registry -> A-Jatin/Assay/TrustMesh source lineage -> Qatoto/Trenova version authority -> Kareya/port-billing rerating -> discrepancy/settlement proof. Model extraction must remain advisory until source-grounded review.
- Value score: A 3/5; B 4/5; C 4/5; D 5/5; E 3/5; F 1/5 = **20/30**.
- Next action: Hunt for an explicitly licensed public-tariff source monitor/parser; meanwhile implement only the generic source-URL/hash/effective-date registry from first principles and require verified document lineage before any dollar finding.

### adonayjunior/tos-integration-service — MIT TOS event normalization/dedup harness
- URL: https://github.com/adonayjunior/tos-integration-service
- Exact commit / revision: `770d671df9111893c4af2b39250ab4f461020cec`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: watch
- What it contains: A generic Spring Boot/Groovy webhook service that maps an explicitly invented TOS event shape into a canonical `TerminalEvent`, normalizes event-code synonyms and container numbers, parses/rejects timestamps, deduplicates retries by `messageId`, and publishes through an abstraction designed for in-memory or Kafka/RabbitMQ implementations. The repository reports 21 tests including HTTP round trips for valid, duplicate, unknown-event and missing-field cases.
- Rare or undernoticed value: A lawful, explicitly non-proprietary test/integration substrate for terminal-event evidence. It helps test whether billing/recovery logic survives source vocabulary variation and webhook retries without double-counting events.
- Likely buyer / user: Terminal/port integration teams, NVOCCs, forwarders and freight software vendors.
- Monetization mechanism: Paid TOS integration implementation when a pilot needs it; otherwise benchmark infrastructure rather than a standalone product.
- Likely first paid wedge: Normalize one authorized terminal event feed into a canonical event stream that downstream free-time/billing logic can consume idempotently.
- Build-time or data advantage: Several weeks to 1–2 months of event-normalization/dedup/integration plumbing.
- Concrete evidence inspected: exact initial commit, README, build/test inventory and actual MIT LICENSE content contained in the commit. The README explicitly says the event vocabulary/message shape are invented and not copied from a proprietary TOS.
- License / rights: MIT verified from the repository commit/license content.
- Reuse classification: Directly reusable under MIT notice requirements; real TOS adapters/message definitions require separate authorization and terms review.
- Why it is not already obvious / crowded: Very small generic integration repo; freight-recovery value emerges only when paired with terminal billing and event-based free-time evidence.
- Combination opportunities: TOS event normalization -> Opstrax/TrustMesh evidence lineage -> port-billing/Qatoto/Trenova tariff authority -> container-charge discrepancy. Also useful as a synthetic source in CI.
- Value score: A 2/5; B 3/5; C 4/5; D 4/5; E 4/5; F 5/5 = **22/30**.
- Next action: Keep as a benchmark/integration watch; do not displace Opstrax. Pull forward only if a paid pilot needs webhook/TOS normalization.
